cafes.name: Emerald Tavern Games & Cafe
cafes.address: 9012 Research Blvd, Ste C1, Austin, TX 78758
cafes.description: Austin's original board game cafe, open since 2013, pairing a library of 100+ tabletop games with gourmet coffee, tea, wine, beer, and pub fare inside an English Tudor-themed space.
cafes.sourceNote: Verified via the business's own site (emeraldtaverngames.com), which lists the address and describes the coffee/tea/wine/beer/pub-fare model. Corroborated by its Yelp listing (347 photos, 276 reviews as of Jul 2026) and an Austin Chronicle feature, "The Best Places to Play Board Games in Austin."

cafes.name: Vigilante Gastropub & Games
cafes.address: 7010 Easy Wind Dr, Ste 150, Austin, TX 78752
cafes.description: A gastropub near Crestview Station built around modern board games, with purpose-built gaming tables that include drink holders and meeple trays, a full cocktail bar, and a scratch kitchen.
cafes.sourceNote: Address confirmed via the official Wizards of the Coast store locator (locator.wizards.com/store/21862) and cross-checked against Yelp. Business model and food/drink offering confirmed on vigilantebar.com and in Austin Chronicle / Smart City Locating local coverage.

cafes.name: Mox Boarding House (Seattle)
cafes.description: A 10,000+ sq ft board game store, restaurant, and bar in Ballard, the original Card Kingdom location rebranded as Mox in 2017, offering a free game library, house-made food, and rotating beer taps.
cafes.sourceNote: Verified via moxboardinghouse.com (Seattle location page) and local news coverage of the 2017 Card Kingdom-to-Mox rebrand (My Ballard, Westside Seattle). Address corroborated by its Yelp listing (591 reviews as of Aug 2026).

cafes.name: Meeples Games
cafes.address: 3727 California Ave SW, Ste 2B, Seattle, WA 98116
cafes.description: A family-owned tabletop game store and cafe in West Seattle's Alaska Junction, offering a rental game library alongside local food, beer, and wine.
cafes.sourceNote: Verified via meeplesgames.com. Corroborated by its Yelp listing (100 reviews) and the West Seattle Chamber of Commerce member directory.

cafes.name: The Missing Piece
cafes.address: 4707 California Ave SW, Ste B, Seattle, WA 98116
cafes.description: A West Seattle game cafe and lounge with 200+ games free to play, local craft coffee and tea, and made-to-order cafe food, styled as a neighborhood living room for gamers.
cafes.sourceNote: Verified directly via themissingpiecegames.com, which lists the address, hours, and food/game offerings. Corroborated by a West Seattle Blog sponsor announcement (Dec 2020) and Yelp.

cafes.name: Raygun Lounge
cafes.address: 501 E Pine St, Retail B, Seattle, WA 98122
cafes.description: A Capitol Hill dive bar, pinball arcade, and board game library rolled into one, with large well-lit tables built for tabletop play alongside classic arcade cabinets.
cafes.sourceNote: Verified via raygunlounge.com and its Wikipedia entry. Address corroborated by Yelp (123 reviews) and the EverOut Seattle venue directory.

cafes.name: U Wine Bar
cafes.description: A wine-focused board game bar in Wallingford, pairing a curated list of wine, beer, cider, and mead with a shelf of board games available to play in-house or take home.
cafes.sourceNote: Address and business model verified via the official Wizards of the Coast store locator (locator.wizards.com/store/17665) and the Eat Local First Seattle business directory. Corroborated by Yelp (14 reviews) and The Infatuation's Seattle review. No standalone business website was found (Instagram: @uwinebar); the field is left blank rather than guessed, per sourcing rules.

cafes.name: Bonus Round Game Cafe
cafes.description: A Lakeview cafe with a curated library of modern board games, staff who teach and recommend titles, and a full menu of coffee, tea, beer, wine, and cocktails.
cafes.sourceNote: Verified via bonusroundcafe.com. Corroborated by Block Club Chicago's 2021 reopening coverage and the Lakeview East Chamber of Commerce member directory.

cafes.name: Athena Board Game Cafe
cafes.description: A Rogers Park board game cafe, reopened in late 2024 at the former Heartland Cafe site, serving an elevated comfort-food menu alongside a rotating library of games for a flat cover charge.
cafes.sourceNote: Verified via athenabgc.com (menu, hours, address). Corroborated by Block Club Chicago's November 2024 reopening story and its current Yelp listing.

cafes.name: Snakes & Lattes Chicago
cafes.description: A Logan Square/Bucktown board game cafe with 800+ games, a full bar and kitchen, and themed private rooms; the Toronto-based chain took over this space from Cards Against Humanity's original Chicago Board Game Cafe in 2020.
cafes.sourceNote: Verified via snakesandlattes.com/chicago for current address, hours, and offerings. The 2020 change of ownership from the original Chicago Board Game Cafe is confirmed via a GlobeNewswire press release, which is why that earlier business name (now closed per Yelp) is not used as the listing name.

cafes.name: Stay & Play Game Cafe
cafes.address: 3932 W Irving Park Rd, Chicago, IL 60618
cafes.description: A Puerto Rican family-owned cafe in Irving Park pairing 700+ board games with jibaritos, tostones, plantains, and rum-based cocktails.
cafes.sourceNote: Verified via stayandplaygamecafe.com. Corroborated by Block Club Chicago's January 2023 feature story and its Yelp listing.

cafes.name: Hex & Company (Upper West Side)
cafes.description: The Upper West Side location of NYC's Hex & Co tabletop cafe chain, combining a full cafe/bar menu with trading card tournaments, D&D and RPG programming, and open board game play.
cafes.sourceNote: Sourced from a Google Maps listing (Apify Google Maps Scraper run, board game cafe search, New York metro). Verified via hexnyc.com, which confirms the food/drink-plus-tabletop model across Hex & Co's Manhattan locations.

cafes.name: Hex & Company (Upper East Side)
cafes.description: The Upper East Side sister location of Hex & Co, offering the same cafe/bar-plus-tabletop-gaming model as the chain's West Side location, with trading card and RPG events.
cafes.sourceNote: Sourced from a Google Maps listing (Apify Google Maps Scraper run, board game cafe search, New York metro). Verified via hexnyc.com, which lists this as one of Hex & Co's three Manhattan locations.

cafes.name: Chaotic Good Cafe
cafes.description: An Upper West Side board game cafe serving specialty coffee, frappes, and treats alongside a board game library, with recurring Mahjong Mondays, D&D sessions, and wine-and-board-game pairing nights.
cafes.sourceNote: Sourced from a Google Maps listing (Apify Google Maps Scraper run, board game cafe search, New York metro). Verified via chaoticgoodcafe.com, which describes the coffee-plus-tabletop-gaming model and its recurring game-night programming.

cafes.name: Coral Sword
cafes.description: An East End Houston neighborhood board game cafe, co-founded in 2018 by Greenway Coffee's David Buehrer with former Houston Astro Hunter Pence and Ming Chen, serving coffee, tea, beer, wine, and pizza alongside an unlimited board game library.
cafes.sourceNote: Sourced from a Google Maps listing (Apify Google Maps Scraper run, board game cafe search, Houston metro). Corroborated by Houstonia Magazine's 2018 opening feature and Sprudge Coffee's coverage of the cafe's coffee-plus-games model.

cafes.name: Board Room
cafes.description: A Dupont Circle bar operating since 2012 as "DC's original board game bar," pairing a full craft beer and cocktail program with an extensive game closet of vintage and modern board games plus classic arcade cabinets.
cafes.sourceNote: Sourced from a Google Maps listing (Apify Google Maps Scraper run, board game cafe search, Washington DC metro). Corroborated by HuffPost DC's 2013 opening coverage and boardroomdc.com describing the games-plus-bar concept.

cafes.name: The Board and Brew
cafes.description: A University City cafe and restaurant with a large curated board game library spanning party, strategy, and dexterity games, serving breakfast through dinner with specialty coffee, craft beer, and cocktails; playing games carries no fee if you're just there to eat.
cafes.sourceNote: Sourced from a Google Maps listing (Apify Google Maps Scraper run, board game cafe search, Philadelphia metro). Verified via theboardandbrew.com, which details the full food menu and game-library model.

cafes.name: BUBS
cafes.address: 102 W Berks St Retail 1, Philadelphia, PA 19122
cafes.description: A Kensington board game cafe named for its home under the Berks Street station (Breakfast/Boardgames Under Berks Station), open late as a sober-friendly "third space" with light snacks and drinks alongside a rotating board game library.
cafes.sourceNote: Sourced from a Google Maps listing (Apify Google Maps Scraper run, board game cafe search, Philadelphia metro). Corroborated by boardgamecafebar.com's directory listing and Philadelphia.Today's August 2025 feature on the Kensington opening.

cafes.name: Queen & Rook
cafes.description: A South Street board game venue with 2,500+ games and staff "Gamekeepers" who help guests pick titles, charging per-person admission for timed play sessions alongside a full restaurant menu and bar plus a retro arcade.
cafes.sourceNote: Sourced from a Google Maps listing (Apify Google Maps Scraper run, board game cafe search, Philadelphia metro). Verified via queenandrookcafe.com, which details the admission-based gaming model, restaurant menu, and bar.

cafes.name: Tavern of Tales
cafes.description: A Mission Hill venue billed as "Boston's Only Board Game Cafe & Bar," offering free-play access to a curated game shelf, private soundproofed game rooms with expanded libraries, a full bar and kitchen, and organized D&D, Magic, and trivia events.
cafes.sourceNote: Sourced from a Google Maps listing (Apify Google Maps Scraper run, board game cafe search, Boston metro). Verified via tavernoftales.com, which brands the venue explicitly as Boston's only board game cafe and bar.

cafes.name: The Game Parlour
cafes.description: An Inner Sunset board game cafe offering hundreds of games for a $7 unlimited-play fee, serving a waffle-centric food menu alongside specialty coffee, milkshakes, beer, and wine.
cafes.sourceNote: Sourced from a Google Maps listing (Apify Google Maps Scraper run, board game cafe search, San Francisco metro). Verified via thegameparlour.com, which details the $7 gaming fee, waffle menu, and coffee/beer/wine bar.

cafes.name: No Land Beyond
cafes.description: A Station North board game bar, shop, and event venue with a 300+ game library, a curated craft beer and cocktail program, and a food menu, explicitly inviting guests to "hang out, eat, drink, and game."
cafes.sourceNote: Sourced from a Google Maps listing (Apify Google Maps Scraper run, board game cafe search, Baltimore metro). Verified via nolandbaltimore.com, which describes the combined game library, bar, and food menu.

cafes.name: Game n' Grounds
cafes.description: A San Fernando Valley cafe in Chatsworth pairing coffee, wine, and beer with a library of 200+ board games, open daily from breakfast through dinner with paninis, crepes, and breakfast fare, plus weekly trivia and open mic nights.
cafes.sourceNote: Google Maps listing (Apify Google Maps Scraper, deeper follow-up run at maxCrawledPlacesPerSearch 50 after the original Los Angeles pull hit 15/15 with no survivors, board game cafe search). Verified via gamengrounds.com, which confirms the coffee/wine/beer-plus-200+-game-library model, food menu, and Chatsworth address.

cafes.name: Forks & Boards
cafes.address: 1818 W Bell Rd Ste 116, Phoenix, AZ 85023
cafes.description: A veteran-owned North Phoenix restaurant and full bar pairing a largely gluten-free menu with a free, rotating library of tabletop games, plus themed prix-fixe "Chef's Movie Night" dinners.
cafes.sourceNote: Google Maps listing (Apify Google Maps Scraper, deeper follow-up run at maxCrawledPlacesPerSearch 50 after the original Phoenix pull hit 15/15 with no survivors, board game cafe search). Verified via forksandboards.com, which confirms the full-bar/gluten-free-menu-plus-tabletop-game-library model.
